newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK STOCKS SHED 1.41PCT, MOMENTUM WEAKENING.
newsitem.headline: GREEK STOCKS SHED 1.41PCT, MOMENTUM WEAKENING.

text.p: Greek stocks fielded a drop on Wednesday in subdued trading with industrials, construction and banks showing signs of weakness.
Brokers said equities were losing momentum as investors were ruffled by fears of resurging inflation.

"Shares seem to have lost momentum and it would take a great deal of positive news to lift them from the 1,400-1,550 trading range in the coming two months," said Yiannis Kalogerakis, broker at ABN AMRO-Axias Securities.
"The market was affected today by fears of a spike in June consumer price inflation and prospects of a stagnant CPI for the rest of the year," he added.
Wednesday's financial press reported that June CPI inflation, expected to be officially released in coming days, would pick up to 5.6 percent from May's 5.4 percent.
Sentiment was also seen dented by reports of financial difficulties faced by small-league brokers.
FTSE International and the Athens stock exchange introduced on Tuesday a new 20-share Greek stock index, FTSE/ASE 20, designed to support derivatives.
It will be officially launched September 24, tracking the performance of the investible market in Athens through the monitoring of 20 of the largest and most liquid Greek stocks.
"There was a beacon of light from the introduction of the new index of select Greek stocks," Kalogerakis said.
"The new index is expected to raise exposure of prime Athens bourse listings to institutional portfolios, also contributing to small investor confidence," he added.
The Athens general index lost 1.41 percent or 21.48 points closing at 1,503.59 from Tuesday's 1,525.07 near the day's lows.
Industrials softened 1.77 percent. Banks and construction retreated 1.06 percent with other sectors posting milder losses.
Turnover was subdued, reaching 10.8 billion drachmas on volume of 3.4 million shares.
Decliners led advancers 143 to 51 with 29 shares unchanged on 223 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted at London's SEAQ International market at $11.50-$11.90. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,112-1,142 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,109-1,169 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying instrument were down 130 drachmas at 6,370.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted at 560.37-596.14 drachmas. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $65.08-$66.77. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 2,927-3,138 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $9.91-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 188-219 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
